title: SledgeHammer: Scalable, Collaborative, Physical Design Flow Orchestration for Agile Hardware Teams | EECS at UC Berkeley
content: SledgeHammer: Scalable, Collaborative, Physical Design Flow Orchestration for Agile Hardware Teams | EECS at UC Berkeley SledgeHammer: Scalable, Collaborative, Physical Design Flow Orchestration for Agile Hardware Teams Andre Green EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley Technical Report No. UCB/EECS-2025-206 December 18, 2025 http://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/2025/EECS-2025-206.pdf The increasing complexity of system-on-chip (SoC) and system-in-package (SiP) designs, together with the impact of shrinking technology nodes, has amplified the need for more flexible, scalable, and efficient physical design flows. To address the limitations of existing physical design (PD) flow tools, we present SledgeHammer, the next generation of the Hammer PD framework that incorporates principled workflow orchestration, improves modularity, and enables collaborative physical design. I implemented a directed acyclic graph (DAG) driven model to replace Hammerâs rigid, timestamp-based build system for more fine-grained dependency management and customizable flow execution. SledgeHammer supports a shared VLSI workspace with a web-based graphical user interface (GUI), enabling real-time flow visualization, parseable logging and relevant metric tracking, along with providing a multi-user collaborative workspace. Through integration with the Chipyard SoC design environment, SledgeHammer has been validated on designs across various nodes, from 130nm to 16nm, including the Rocket 5-stage RISC-V in-order scalar core and a chiplet with UCIe interfaces. Our results establish that SledgeHammer introduces negligible scheduling overhead, which consistently fell below 1% of the total runtime of the flow. This included an average queue time per PD stage of less than 6.22 seconds per module, with upmost of 22% reductions in runtime during parameter sweeps by eliminating unnecessary stage execution. We demonstrate how SledgeHammer reduces redundant computation, streamlines debugging, and enables future enhancements such as cloud deployment, advanced checkpointing, and further support for large-scale SoCs and SiPs. By bridging modern workflow orchestration with physical design, SledgeHammer redefines the possibilities of VLSI development, empowering teams to collaborate more effectively and build the next generation of SoCs and SiPs.
